description: A single-panel scatter plot (no sub-panels). The y-axis is specific energy absorption E_spec in J/mm³, ticked 0.0 to 0.6 in 0.1 steps; the x-axis is aluminium content in wt.%, ticked 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11. Both axes carry axis-break symbols (//), on x just above 6 and on y near 0.2. Open teal squares, keyed in the legend as "Fe-Mn-Al-C-alloys", occupy the upper band: two points at low Al, just above the 6 wt.% tick, fall between the 0.2 and 0.3 y-ticks and just above 0.3; further points between about 7.4 and 10.5 wt.% Al lie predominantly between the 0.4 and 0.5 y-ticks, with the densest cluster spread between the 8 and 9 wt.% Al ticks; the single highest point sits between the 0.5 and 0.6 y-ticks near 11 wt.% Al. Four open grey squares lie at low Al (~6.2–6.3 wt.%) and low E_spec, near the 0.15–0.20 level, arrow-labelled "high strength IF steel", "HC300LA - ZStE300" and "DC04 - FeP04" (conventional deep-drawing steels). The legend also lists deformation rates 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ and 10⁻³ s⁻¹. The figure demonstrates that Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys absorb far more specific energy per volume than conventional deep-drawing steels.

subfigures.description: One scatter plot: specific energy absorption E_spec [J/mm³] (y, 0.0–0.6) versus aluminium content [wt.%] (x, 6–11), both axes broken. Teal open squares = 'Fe-Mn-Al-C-alloys' at high E_spec; four grey open squares at ~6.2–6.3 wt.% Al and low E_spec, arrow-labelled 'high strength IF steel', 'HC300LA - ZStE300', 'DC04 - FeP04'. Legend notes deformation rates 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ and 10⁻³ s⁻¹.

observations.observation: The figure is a single scatter plot with specific energy absorption E_spec [J/mm³] on the y-axis (ticked 0.0 to 0.6 in 0.1 steps) and aluminium content [wt.%] on the x-axis (ticked 6 to 11).
Axis-break symbols (//) appear on both axes: on the x-axis just above the 6 wt.% tick and on the y-axis near 0.2 J/mm³.
Open teal squares are identified in the legend as 'Fe-Mn-Al-C-alloys' and occupy the upper part of the plot.

Four open grey squares lie at low aluminium content (about 6.2–6.3 wt.%) and low E_spec (near the 0.15–0.20 J/mm³ level), and three of them are indicated by arrows labelled 'high strength IF steel', 'HC300LA - ZStE300' and 'DC04 - FeP04'.
Every Fe-Mn-Al-C point lies above the 0.2 J/mm³ y-tick, whereas every conventional deep-drawing steel point lies at or below about 0.20 J/mm³, so the two groups do not overlap in E_spec.
The highest point in the figure (Fe-Mn-Al-C alloy, near 11 wt.% Al) lies between the 0.5 and 0.6 J/mm³ y-ticks; the second-highest group sits just above the 0.5 tick near 9.5 wt.% Al.

The legend lists two deformation rates, '10⁻⁴ s⁻¹' and '10⁻³ s⁻¹', both drawn with open-square marker keys, so the assignment of marker type to deformation rate cannot be resolved from the legend alone.
The Fe-Mn-Al-C data span roughly 6.6 to 11 wt.% Al, with the most crowded cluster lying between the 8 and 9 wt.% Al ticks and between the 0.4 and 0.5 J/mm³ y-ticks.
The caption states that the plotted values are specific energy absorption values of selected Fe-Mn-Al-C steels in comparison with different conventional deep-drawing steels (Color figure online).

The citing text asserts that alloys based on the austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C system are most attractive because of their superior strain hardening, high energy absorption (Fig. 2) and high density reduction.
The citing text states that some of the data shown in Figs. 1 and 2 stem from the work of the late Professor Georg Frommeyer.
No numeric value is printed next to any data point; all values are read as positions relative to the axis ticks.

exact aluminium contents of the Fe-Mn-Al-C points cannot be read precisely because the x-axis is broken just above 6 wt.% and points are unlabelled
number of overlapping points within the 8–9 wt.% Al cluster cannot be counted reliably
